text:
katie_support: Customer escalation (ACME) — after today's canary they say our API is either not making the tool call or the tool gets the wrong arg order. They gave two failing examples and a repro. Ticket: #INC-12345. Anyone oncall?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: router-service v2.14.0 -> 10% traffic at 2026-03-17T09:12:00Z (commit: fc3a9b2). Config change: 'tool-mapping' key rename in router config.

katie_support: Pasted minimal repro from customer (sanitized):
```json
POST /v1/respond
{
  "input": "charge customer",
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "charge_card",
    "args": {"amount": 49.99, "customer_id": "ACME-456"}
  }
}
```
Customer says expected tool invocation: charge_card(amount=49.99, customer_id="ACME-456")
But server logs show: 
```
tool_invoked: charge_card args: ["ACME-456", 49.99]
```
and in other case there was no tool_invoked at all (returned fallback text).

katie_support: They started seeing this at ~09:20 UTC, shortly after the canary.

dave_platform: Can you paste the router log lines around the request id? Any sign of a mapping lookup failure? Also which model/variant?

katie_support: Model: gpt-redwood-compat-v1 (variant B). Request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Logs: (trimmed)
```
2026-03-17T09:20:12Z INFO router: routing request r-0a1b2c3d -> backend: serve-07
2026-03-17T09:20:12Z DEBUG mapper: tool-key resolved to "charge_card_v2"
2026-03-17T09:20:12Z DEBUG serializer: serializing args for tool charge_card_v2 -> ["ACME-456", 49.99]
2026-03-17T09:20:12Z INFO runtime: called tool charge_card_v2 (success)
```

katie_support: That serializer line is suspicious — customer says we used to send a dict (named args). Now it looks like an ordered list.

sophie_ml: This smells like the rename in router config. If the router maps to charge_card_v2 but the tool signature changed (expected named args) and our serializer started using positional output for backward compatibility, positional order can be wrong if key ordering changed. Any recent change to arg-serialization?

mohit_sre: I can check deploy diff. From the deploy notes the router config rename moved tool ids under a nested map and I see a small helper that flattens args into a list when the tool mapping has `legacyOrder: true`. Maybe the config flip toggled legacyOrder by mistake for some mappings.

mohit_sre: Running quick grep... found router config delta: 
```diff
- "charge_card": { "id": "charge_card_v1", "accepts_named_args": true }
+ "charge_card": { "id": "charge_card_v2", "legacyOrder": true }
```

mohit_sre: I'm going to roll the canary back to 0% for router-service now to confirm.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated for router-service v2.14.0 -> 0% at 2026-03-17T09:25:10Z

mohit_sre: Rollback complete. Routing traffic back to v2.13.8.

katie_support: Pushed a quick note to ACME to test again. They replied: "we retried and tool calls look correct now, no missing calls, args are named again. Thanks." :thumbsup:

sophie_ml: Root cause summary: accidental config rename during canary changed tool-mapping metadata (added legacyOrder=true) causing serializer to emit positional arg list in a different order. For tools that expect named kwargs this caused argument swap or misbind.

katie_support: Customer satisfied for now. Filing followup: engineering should add a config validation that flags conflicting flags (legacyOrder vs accepts_named_args) and a regression test that runs our tool-call end-to-end during canary. Assigning to @dave_platform and @sophie_ml to triage and patch.

dave_platform: Will add a validation in router config loader and a canary smoke test that asserts tool-call roundtrip preserves arg names. Also we'll audit mappings touched in the release.

katie_support: Thanks everyone — closing customer loop. Ticket updated and customer notified.

mohit_sre: Adding postmortem note for the release: include checklist to verify mapping metadata.

katie_support: (reaction) :white_check_mark:
